task_message:
Case M40: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 220x220x406 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case M40 complete.

**Summary:** The myxoid soft-tissue tumor was found as a large, lobulated T2-hyperintense mass in the lateral aspect of the (right) proximal thigh. I seeded it with points on the bright core, outlined the full lesion (including the lower/medial lobule) on the axial slice where it is largest, and refined the boundary. The final mask is one connected component of **62.1 mL** (extent ~69 × 56 × 41 mm, axial 301–369).

Key judgment calls:
- **Included:** the entire heterogeneous, lobulated hyperintense mass with its less intense periphery, matching the visible tumor margin in axial, coronal and sagittal planes.
- **Excluded:** the striking peritumoral edema/fascial "tail" running along the fascia (adding it flooded the mask to ~204 mL and it was clearly streaky fluid), plus the automatic candidates C1–C5, which were subcutaneous fat/edema crescents and tiny non-contiguous foci.

Confidence is medium because the tumor–edema transition at the posterior/inferior margin is gradual, but the outline follows a consistent edge on all three planes.
